context.guidance: Erase Personal Data once its Purpose is served, by wiring erasure into account-closure and end-of-purpose events rather than leaving the records in place. §8(7)(a) is the erasure duty this Issue Type cites for that case. Where Rule 8(1) applies to a Third Schedule class, schedule the erasure job from the retention period the Third Schedule sets.

value.fix: The supplied evidence (`paranoid: true,`) is a bare configuration flag and does not itself retain Personal Data, so the RET-01 fix belongs where this setting governs personal-data storage. (1) Trace where the flag is read and which records it affects. (2) Add an erasure handler subscribed to account-closure and end-of-purpose events that deletes or irreversibly anonymises Personal Data once its purpose is served, per §8(7)(a) of the DPDP Act 2023, instead of leaving the records in place. (3) For data classes under Rule 8(1), take the retention period from the Third Schedule and schedule an erasure job (cron or queue) that removes records when that period expires. (4) Log erasure outcomes for audit, and extend erasure to backups, replicas, and downstream processors. (5) Add tests showing that closing an account or ending a purpose triggers erasure, and that scheduled jobs delete records past their retention period.
